243: static void hal_hci_driver_send(uint8_t *buf, uint16_t len)
244: {
245:     uint8_t type = buf[0];
246:     int32_t ret = 0;
247:     //LOGD("type %d,len %d", type, len);
248: 
249:     switch (type)
250:     {
251:     case DATA_TYPE_COMMAND:
252:     {
253:         uint16_t opcode = (((uint16_t)buf[2]) << 8 | buf[1]);
254:         uint8_t dir = hal_hci_arb_cmd_dir(s_controller_mode, opcode);
255: 
256:         switch (dir)
257:         {
258:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_DIR_PRI:
259:             bk_ble_hci_cmd_to_controller(&buf[1], len - 1);
260:             break;
261: 
262:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_DIR_SEC:
263:             ble_hci_to_secondary_controller(buf, len);
264:             break;
265: 
266:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_DIR_ALL:
267:         {
268:             //todo: add to pending list
269:             multi_ct_cmd_t msg = {0};
270:             msg.opcode = opcode;
271:             msg.vote = 0;
272: 
273:             ret = rtos_push_to_queue(&s_multi_controller_cmd_queue, &msg, BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER);
274: 
275:             if (ret)
276:             {
277:                 LOGE("push to queue err 0x%04x", opcode);
278:                 BK_ASSERT(0);
279:             }
280: 
281:             bk_ble_hci_cmd_to_controller(&buf[1], len - 1);
282:             ble_hci_to_secondary_controller(buf, len);
283:         }
284:         break;
285: 
286:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_DIR_NOT_SURE:
287:             if (opcode == APP_HCI_DISCONNECT_CMD_OPCODE
288:                     || opcode == APP_HCI_VENDOR_SET_ACL_PRIORITY_CMD_OPCODE
289:                     || opcode == APP_HCI_RD_FAIL_CONTACT_CNT_CMD_OPCODE
290:                     || opcode == APP_HCI_RST_FAIL_CONTACT_CNT_CMD_OPCODE
291:                     || opcode == APP_HCI_RD_LINK_QUAL_CMD_OPCODE
292:                     || opcode == APP_HCI_RD_RSSI_CMD_OPCODE
293:                     || opcode == APP_HCI_RD_AFH_CH_MAP_CMD_OPCODE
294:                     || opcode == APP_HCI_RD_CLK_CMD_OPCODE
295:                     || opcode == APP_HCI_RD_ENC_KEY_SIZE_CMD_OPCODE)
296:             {
297:                 uint16_t acl_handle = (((uint16_t)buf[5]) << 8 | buf[4]);
298: 
299:                 if (s_secondary_cb && s_secondary_cb->send &&
300:                         acl_handle >= s_secondary_cb->acl_handle_threshold_min && acl_handle <= s_secondary_cb->acl_handle_threshold_max)
301:                 {
302:                     ble_hci_to_secondary_controller(buf, len);
303:                 }
304:                 else
305:                 {
306:                     bk_ble_hci_cmd_to_controller(&buf[1], len - 1);
307:                 }
308:             }
309:             else
310:             {
311:                 LOGE("unknow how to send op 0x%x dir %d type %d !!!", opcode, dir, hci_cmd_get_type(opcode));
312:             }
313: 
314:             break;
315:         }
316:     }
317:     break;
318: 
319:     case DATA_TYPE_ACL:
320:     {
321:         switch (s_controller_mode)
322:         {
323:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_MODE_PRI_ALL_SEC_NONE:
324:             bk_ble_hci_acl_to_controller(&buf[1], len - 1);
325:             break;
326: 
327:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_MODE_PRI_NONE_SEC_ALL:
328:              ble_hci_to_secondary_controller(buf, len);
329: 
330:             break;
331: 
332:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_MODE_PRI_BLE_SEC_BT:
333:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_MODE_PRI_BT_SEC_BLE:
334:         {
335:             uint16_t acl_handle = (((uint16_t)buf[2]) << 8 | buf[1]);
336: 
337:             if (s_secondary_cb && s_secondary_cb->send &&
338:                     acl_handle >= s_secondary_cb->acl_handle_threshold_min && acl_handle <= s_secondary_cb->acl_handle_threshold_max)
339:             {
340:                 ble_hci_to_secondary_controller(buf, len);
341:             }
342:             else
343:             {
344:                 bk_ble_hci_acl_to_controller(&buf[1], len - 1);
345:             }
346:         }
347:         break;
348:         }
349:     }
350:     break;
351: 
352:     case DATA_TYPE_SCO:
353:     {
354:         switch (s_controller_mode)
355:         {
356:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_MODE_PRI_ALL_SEC_NONE:
357:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_MODE_PRI_BT_SEC_BLE:
358:             bk_ble_hci_to_controller(DATA_TYPE_SCO, &buf[1], len - 1);
359:             break;
360: 
361:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_MODE_PRI_NONE_SEC_ALL:
362:         case MULTI_CONTROLLER_MODE_PRI_BLE_SEC_BT:
363:             ble_hci_to_secondary_controller(buf, len);
364:             break;
365:         }
366:     }
367:     break;
368: 
369:     default:
370:         LOGE("unknown type (0x%x)", type);
371:         break;
372:     }
373: }

# BK7258 Bluetooth transport implementation map

Read-only exploration completed. The repository contains:

1. A formal contest-side BK7258 MBOX0/“Mailbox V2” transport used by OpenVela AP/CPU1.
2. A vendor Armino logical-mailbox implementation used by AP/CPU1 and CP/CPU0.
3. Vendor AP/CP Bluetooth IPC code built on `MB_CHNL_BT_CMD`.
4. No completed Bluetooth adapter in the formal contest transport: the formal channel tables currently cover hardware control, PWC, Wi-Fi, UART, and SARADC, but not Bluetooth.

The key conclusion is that the Bluetooth transport should use the existing 16-byte MBOX V2 descriptor as a raw overlay of Armino’s 16-byte `hci_hdr_t`/`mb_chnl_cmd_t`, while preserving the vendor pointer-passing ownership protocol.

---

## 1. CPU and direction model

| Side | CPU | Vendor logical-channel direction | Bluetooth channel |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| OpenVela AP | CPU1 | CPU1 → CPU0 | `MB_CHNL_BT_CMD = 0x13` |
| Armino CP | CPU0 | CPU0 → CPU1 | `MB_CHNL_BT_CMD = 0x43` |

The AP-side channel enum starts at `CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(CPU1, CPU0) = 0x10`; Bluetooth is the fourth logical channel, `0x13`. The CP-side enum starts at `CPX_LOG_CHNL_START(CPU0, CPU1) = 0x40`; Bluetooth is `0x43`.

Vendor definitions:

- AP channel: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:77-99`
- CP channel: `/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:64-86`

The formal contest transport currently defines:

- AP/CPU1 transmit channels:
  - `0x10` HW_CTRL
  - `0x12` PWC
  - `0x14` Wi-Fi command
  - `0x15` Wi-Fi data
  - `0x19` UART0
- CPU0/CP-to-AP receive channels:
  - `0x42` PWC
  - `0x44` Wi-Fi command
  - `0x45` Wi-Fi data
  - `0x49` UART0
  - `0x4c` SARADC

See `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:73-86`.

There is currently no `0x13` or `0x43` in those formal arrays. The required Bluetooth additions are therefore:

```c
#define BK7258_MB_CHAN_BT_CMD_TX  0x13u
#define BK7258_MB_CHAN_BT_CMD_RX  0x43u
```

and corresponding additions to the formal transport’s TX/RX channel tables.

---

# 2. Formal contest mailbox implementation

## 2.1 Public ABI and wire structures

Primary header:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_mbox.h`

Important definitions:

- Physical mailbox constants and registers: lines `15-42`
- Message size and header masks: lines `44-66`
- Control/state constants: lines `68-71`
- Existing logical channel constants: lines `73-86`
- Shared CP/AP memory map: lines `88-124`
- 16-byte wire descriptor: lines `126-149`
- Header accessor/maker functions: lines `151-195`
- Link-state enum and callback types: lines `217-235`
- Physical APIs: lines `237-243`
- Formal logical mailbox APIs: lines `245-260`
- Compatibility APIs and UART APIs: lines `262-290`

The formal wire descriptor is:

```c
struct bk7258_mb_wire_message
{
  uint32_t header;          /* offset 0 */
  uint32_t payload_address; /* offset 4 */
  uint16_t payload_length;  /* offset 8 */
  uint8_t  flags;           /* offset 10 */
  uint8_t  crc8;            /* offset 11 */
  uint32_t reserved;        /* offset 12 */
};
```

It is exactly 16 bytes. The repository asserts every offset and the total size at:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:126-149`.

### Header bit layout

The 32-bit `header` is explicitly defined as:

| Bits | Field |
|---|---|
| `0..7` | command |
| `8..11` | state |
| `12..15` | control |
| `16..23` | sequence |
| `24..31` | logical channel |

Definitions are at:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:44-54`

The formal helper is:

```c
bk7258_mb_make_header(command, state, control, sequence, channel)
```

at:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:186-195`.

Control constants:

```c
BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX = 0x01
BK7258_MB_CTRL_SYNC_TX = 0x02
BK7258_MB_CTRL_RESET   = 0x04
```

Failure state:

```c
BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL = 0x01
```

at:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:68-71`.

---

## 2.2 Physical MBOX0 transport

Source:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c`

Important functions:

| Function | Lines | Role |
|---|---:|---|
| `bk7258_mbox_rx_status` | `40-43` | Reads physical RX status |
| `mbox_clear_errors` | `45-70` | Clears/write-counts mailbox hardware errors |
| `mbox_valid_envelope` | `72-95` | Validates source, length, alignment, and address range |
| `bk7258_mbox_send` | `97-129` | Publishes physical descriptor pointer and length |
| `mbox_alloc_desc` | `131-143` | Allocates local receive descriptor |
| `mbox_priority_message` | `146-152` | Gives ACK/RESET priority |
| `mbox_process_desc` | `177-212` | Dispatches received descriptors |
| `bk7258_mbox_irq` | `214-265` | Drains hardware FIFO and copies messages |
| `bk7258_mbox_set_callback` | `268-271` | Installs logical receive callback |
| `bk7258_mbox_kick_rx` | `273-279` | Synchronously drains RX |
| `bk7258_mbox_discard_deferred` | `281-294` | Drops obsolete deferred ordinary commands |
| `bk7258_mbox_get_stats` | `296-308` | Reads physical diagnostics |
| `bk7258_mbox_init` | `310-345` | Configures registers, IRQ, and FIFO |

### Physical descriptor bytes

`bk7258_mbox_send()` does not copy the 16-byte message into the hardware FIFO. It sends a two-word physical envelope:

```c
wire[0] = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)message;
wire[1] = sizeof(*message);       /* 16 */
bk7258_mbox_send(0, wire);
```

The formal implementation is at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:223-248`

and ultimately stages the words into:

```c
TDATA0 = data[0];
TDATA1 = data[1];
TID    = destination;
```

at:

`.../bk7258_mbox0.c:120-127`.

For AP → CP Bluetooth:

```text
physical data[0] = AP address of 16-byte Bluetooth descriptor
physical data[1] = 0x00000010
destination      = 0 / CPU0
```

For CP → AP, the vendor CP adapter emits the same two-word envelope with a pointer into CP RAM. The CP-side implementation is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:391-446`

and the matching contest external copy is:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:391-446`.

### Receive validation

The formal AP/CPU1 receiver requires:

- physical source CPU `0`
- descriptor length exactly `16`
- 4-byte-aligned descriptor address
- address inside CP RAM

at:

`.../bk7258_mbox0.c:72-95`.

The CP vendor adapter, when receiving AP/CPU1 traffic, requires:

- source CPU `MAILBOX_CPU1`
- length exactly `sizeof(mailbox_data_t)` = 16
- 4-byte alignment
- AP address range `0x28010000..0x28064000`

at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:258-320`.

The contest copy has the same validation at:

`.../external/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:258-320`.

---

## 2.3 Formal logical transport

Source:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c`

Important state and pool definitions:

- TX channels, RX channels, ACK pools, timeout values: lines `24-33`
- Logical channel state: lines `35-49`
- Active transaction: lines `51-61`
- ACK slot: lines `63-68`
- Recovery epoch: lines `70-78`
- Channel arrays and callbacks: lines `105-147`

Current limitations:

```c
#define MB_CHANNEL_COUNT    5u
#define MB_RX_CHANNEL_COUNT 4u
```

at lines `24-25`.

The arrays are:

```c
g_channel_ids[] =
{
  HW_CTRL_TX,
  PWC_TX,
  WIFI_CMD_TX,
  WIFI_DATA_TX,
  UART0_TX
};
```

at lines `105-112`.

```c
g_rx_channel_ids[] =
{
  WIFI_CMD_RX,
  WIFI_DATA_RX,
  UART0_RX,
  SARADC_RX
};
```

at lines `114-120`.

For Bluetooth, append the new channel after UART0 to preserve existing UART assumptions:

```c
g_channel_ids[] =
{
  ...,
  BK7258_MB_CHAN_UART0_TX,
  BK7258_MB_CHAN_BT_CMD_TX
};

g_rx_channel_ids[] =
{
  ...,
  BK7258_MB_CHAN_SARADC_RX,
  BK7258_MB_CHAN_BT_CMD_RX
};
```

The existing code uses `g_channels[4]` as the UART state channel in the probe worker:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:953-965`.

Appending Bluetooth rather than inserting it avoids changing that assumption.

### Send API

```c
int bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(
    uint8_t logical_channel,
    const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
    bk7258_mb_tx_complete_t callback,
    void *arg);
```

Declaration:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:245-251`

Implementation:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1051-1107`.

Semantics:

- Requires `bk7258_mailbox_init()` and `bk7258_mailbox_start()`.
- Rejects `NULL`.
- Rejects unknown logical channel.
- Allows only one queued transaction per logical channel.
- Allows ordinary traffic only while link state is `READY`.
- During `PROBING`, only UART state traffic is allowed.
- Copies the caller’s 16 bytes into persistent channel state.
- The caller’s original `message` does not need to remain alive after return.
- Callback and argument are saved and invoked on completion.

Relevant lines:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1059-1106`.

Return values include:

- `-EAGAIN`: not initialized/started
- `-EINVAL`: unknown channel
- `-EBUSY`: same logical channel already queued
- `-ENOLINK`: link not ready or transaction quarantined
- `OK`: accepted/queued

### Dispatch and serialization

`dispatch_locked()` is at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:428-550`.

Important behavior:

1. Queued ACKs are sent first, before reset or ordinary traffic, lines `438-452`.
2. RESET is sent next, lines `454-465`.
3. Only one ordinary active transaction exists globally, checked at lines `467-470`.
4. Channel traffic is selected in array order, lines `472-528`.
5. The formal transport rewrites the header before sending:

```c
active->message.header = bk7258_mb_make_header(
    bk7258_mb_header_cmd(&channel->pending),
    bk7258_mb_header_state(&channel->pending),
    0,
    ++g_tx_seq,
    g_channel_ids[i]);
```

at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:512-521`.

For Bluetooth, the message must have a valid low-byte command and zero state before dispatch. The transport will add the sequence and channel.

---

# 3. Formal callback and ACK semantics

## 3.1 TX completion callback

Type:

```c
typedef void (*bk7258_mb_tx_complete_t)(
    const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *ack,
    int result,
    void *arg);
```

Declaration:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:226-234`.

The callback is called by:

```c
complete_transaction()
```

at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:286-309`.

Important properties:

- `result == OK` means the transport-level ACK matched.
- `result == -EREMOTEIO` means the peer returned `BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL`.
- The callback receives `NULL` ACK on local abort, timeout, or failed pending transaction.
- The callback executes directly from the mailbox receive processing path.
- Do not block in this callback.
- Do not retain the `ack` pointer after callback return.
- A callback should generally only update state, post a semaphore, or enqueue work.

ACK matching checks:

- active transaction exists
- control exactly `BK7258_MB_CTRL_ACK_BOX`
- logical channel matches
- sequence matches
- command matches

at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:552-584`.

The state may contain only `BK7258_MB_STATE_COM_FAIL`; any other state bits are rejected at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:630-635`.

The normal result calculation is at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:637-644`.

## 3.2 RX callback

Type:

```c
typedef int (*bk7258_mb_channel_rx_t)(
    const struct bk7258_mb_wire_message *message,
    uint8_t *ack_flags,
    void *arg);
```

Declaration:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:226-234`.

Registration:

```c
int bk7258_mailbox_register_rx(
    uint8_t logical_channel,
    bk7258_mb_channel_rx_t callback,
    void *arg);
```

Implementation:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1109-1121`.

For Bluetooth, register a callback on `0x43`.

`handle_command()` is at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:709-815`.

It:

1. Allocates an ACK slot unless `SYNC_TX` is set.
2. Validates control, state, and channel high nibble.
3. Calls the registered RX callback.
4. Treats `-EAGAIN` specially:
   - releases the ACK slot
   - leaves the command deferred
   - returns `-EAGAIN`
5. Converts any other negative callback result into `COM_FAIL`.
6. Generates an ACK with matching command, sequence, and channel.
7. Places `ack_flags` into the ACK’s word at offset 4.
8. Dispatches the ACK.

The relevant code is:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:721-815`.

### Correct Bluetooth RX callback behavior

For a received Bluetooth packet:

- Copy or extract the HCI packet type and pointer immediately.
- Enqueue the pointer to a worker queue.
- Return `OK` only after the queue entry is safely recorded.
- Return `-EAGAIN` if the queue is full, so the formal mailbox retains/defer-retries the command instead of acknowledging and losing ownership.
- Do not free the pointer from the ISR unless the packet is definitively rejected.
- Do not block or allocate large buffers in the callback.

This differs from the vendor implementation, which pushes a small `{type, pointer}` record into a queue from its mailbox RX callback.

Vendor AP RX callback:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:53-143`

Vendor CP RX callback:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:56-146`.

---

# 4. Bluetooth wire format over the 16-byte descriptor

The vendor Bluetooth IPC does not use the formal descriptor fields semantically as `payload_address`, `payload_length`, `flags`, and `reserved`. It uses the same 16 bytes as a raw `hci_hdr_t`/`mb_chnl_cmd_t` overlay.

Vendor definition:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/include/bt_ipc_core.h:58-78`

and the equivalent CP definition:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/include/bt_ipc_core.h:59-78`.

The raw layout is effectively:

| Offset | Bytes | Meaning for Bluetooth |
|---:|---:|---|
| `0` | 4 | Mailbox header |
| `4` | 1 | HCI packet type |
| `5..7` | 3 | padding/alignment |
| `8` | 4 | `hdr_ptr`, a 32-bit cross-core pointer |
| `12..15` | 4 | unused/trailing mailbox words |

The union overlays this with:

```c
mb_chnl_cmd_t
{
    mb_chnl_hdr_t hdr; /* word 0 */
    uint32_t param1;   /* word 1 */
    uint32_t param2;   /* word 2 */
    uint32_t param3;   /* word 3 */
}
```

from:

`.../bt_ipc_core.h:58-78`

and the standard mailbox command structure:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:108-126`.

## HCI packet type constants

Defined at:

`.../bt_ipc_core.h:79-86`

and identical on AP/CP:

```c
HCI_COMMAND_PKT = 0x01
HCI_ACL_DATA_PKT = 0x02
HCI_SCO_DATA_PKT = 0x03
HCI_EVENT_PKT = 0x04
HCI_FREE_PKT = 0x0a
```

These values are carried in byte 4 / word 1 of the raw 16-byte message.

## Example AP → CP HCI command

Assume:

- transport command byte = `0`
- sequence = `S`
- channel = `0x13`
- packet type = `HCI_COMMAND_PKT = 0x01`
- allocated command header pointer = `AP_PTR`
- trailing word = zero

The 16-byte logical payload, in little-endian byte order, is:

```text
offset 0: 00 00 S 13
offset 4: 01 00 00 00
offset 8: AP_PTR[0] AP_PTR[1] AP_PTR[2] AP_PTR[3]
offset 12: 00 00 00 00
```

The first word is the formal header:

```c
bk7258_mb_make_header(0, 0, 0, S, 0x13)
```

The formal TX dispatch rewrites the command/state/control/sequence/channel fields at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:512-521`.

The command body allocated by the vendor AP is:

```c
struct __attribute__((packed)) cmd_hdr_t
{
    uint16_t opcode;
    uint8_t  param_len;
    uint8_t  param[];
};
```

at:

`.../bt_ipc_core.h:30-35`.

The AP allocates and populates it at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:201-223`.

## Example AP → CP ACL packet

The logical descriptor is identical except:

```text
byte 4 = 0x02
word 2  = AP pointer to acl_hdr_t
```

The allocated body is:

```c
struct __attribute__((packed)) acl_hdr_t
{
    uint16_t hdl_flags;
    uint16_t datalen;
    uint8_t  param[];
};
```

at:

`.../bt_ipc_core.h:44-50`.

Allocation and population:

`.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:249-273`.

## Example CP → AP event

The CP sends the same 16-byte raw structure in the opposite logical direction:

```text
header channel = 0x43
byte 4         = 0x04
word 2         = CP_PTR to event_hdr_t
```

The CP allocation is at:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:204-249`.

The event body is:

```c
struct __attribute__((packed)) event_hdr_t
{
    uint8_t event_code;
    uint8_t param_len;
    uint8_t param[];
};
```

at:

`.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/include/bt_ipc_core.h:38-43`.

## HCI FREE packet

After AP consumes a CP-owned event or ACL buffer, it sends:

```text
byte 4 = 0x0a
word 2  = original CP_PTR
```

The AP-side function is:

`.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:297-304`.

The CP receives the pointer as `BT_IPC_FREE_MSG` and frees it at:

`.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:464-469`.

This pointer-release transaction is essential. Without it, every CP-originated event/ACL packet leaks.

# 7. Bluetooth lifecycle and formal-board integration

## Vendor Bluetooth lifecycle

AP public entry points are in:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_avdk_smp/ap/components/bk_bluetooth/api/bt_main.c`

Important functions:

- `bk_enable_bt`: lines `49-61`
- `bk_disable_bt`: lines `63-75`
- `bk_bluetooth_init`: lines `77-156`
- `bk_bluetooth_deinit`: lines `158-216`
- `bk_bluetooth_init_deinit_compelete`: lines `262-268`

`bk_bluetooth_init()` performs:

1. Creates the init/deinit semaphore.
2. Calls `bt_ipc_init()`.
3. Sends vendor opcode INIT.
4. Waits up to 5000 ms for CP’s vendor completion event.
5. Initializes the AP host/HCI path.

at:

`.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/api/bt_main.c:77-156`.

The AP sends INIT as two bytes in big-endian order:

```c
cmd_data[0] = opcode >> 8;
cmd_data[1] = opcode & 0xff;
```

at:

`.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/api/bt_main.c:49-55`.

The CP parses the vendor command as big-endian:

`.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:347-356`.

The CP reports INIT/DEINIT completion as three vendor-event bytes:

```text
opcode low byte
opcode high byte
status
```

at:

`.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:564-570`.

The AP parses those three bytes little-endian at:

`.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:353-364`.

This asymmetry is intentional and must be preserved.

## Formal contest startup

The formal AP initializes the mailbox from:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_serial.c:219-244`.

Sequence:

```c
bk7258_mailbox_init();
bk7258_mb_uart_init();
bk7258_mailbox_start();
bk7258_mb_uart_start();
```

The board bring-up then waits for UART0 mailbox link readiness, starts HW_CTRL heartbeat, starts PWC, and initializes Wi-Fi:

`/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:63-94`.

There is currently no Bluetooth initialization in this sequence. The Bluetooth implementation will need an explicit integration point after the mailbox transport is started and the AP/CP link is ready.

A reasonable lifecycle ordering is:

1. `bk7258_mailbox_init()`
2. Register Bluetooth RX callback for `0x43`
3. `bk7258_mailbox_start()`
4. Wait for `bk7258_mailbox_wait_link_ready()`
5. Initialize the Bluetooth IPC queue/worker
6. Send AP-side vendor INIT through `0x13`
7. Wait for CP vendor INIT-completion event
8. Register/open the AP HCI host path
9. Run normal HCI command/ACL/event traffic
10. On deinit:
   - stop accepting new HCI packets
   - drain/free received CP buffers
   - send vendor DEINIT
   - wait for completion
   - unregister HCI callbacks

The existing vendor implementation does not fully deinitialize the IPC mailbox queue/channel during normal Bluetooth deinit. `bk_bluetooth_deinit()` deinitializes `bt_sem` but does not call a Bluetooth IPC deinit routine:

`.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/api/bt_main.c:158-216`.

That behavior should be consciously preserved or corrected in a formal port; otherwise repeated init/deinit cycles may encounter stale queue, thread, channel, or semaphore state.

# 8. Memory, pointer, cache, and lifetime constraints

## 8.1 Pointer width

The vendor wire structure carries:

```c
uint32_t hdr_ptr;
```

at:

`.../bt_ipc_core.h:58-72`.

The vendor code explicitly casts allocated pointers to 32-bit:

```c
msg.hdr_ptr = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)cmd_hdr;
```

and equivalent event/ACL/SCO paths:

- AP: `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:177-295`
- CP: `.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:180-298`

Therefore:

- Both cores must use a shared 32-bit address map.
- The pointer must be visible and dereferenceable by the receiving core.
- Do not use a pointer to private TCM, inaccessible cache alias, stack, or a region not mapped by the peer.
- Do not assume a 64-bit pointer can be represented.
- The descriptor envelope pointer and the HCI payload pointer are separate pointers.

## 8.2 Physical descriptor memory

The formal transport places active and ACK messages in aligned static storage:

- active message aligned to 32 bytes: `.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:51-61`
- ACK message aligned to 32 bytes: `.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:63-68`
- recovery reset/probe messages aligned to 32 bytes: `.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:70-78`

The physical sender publishes a pointer to that storage rather than copying to a hardware register:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:223-234`.

The receiver copies the 16-byte descriptor before invoking higher-level logic:

`.../bk7258_mbox0.c:246-259`.

Consequently, the formal transport’s `message` pointer passed to an RX callback is a local copied descriptor and is not the original shared slot. It is only valid during callback execution.

## 8.3 HCI payload lifetime

The HCI data itself is not copied into the mailbox descriptor. Only its address is carried.

AP allocation examples:

- commands: `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:201-223`
- events: `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:225-247`
- ACL: `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:249-271`
- SCO: `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:273-295`

CP allocation examples:

- vendor commands/events: `.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:180-250`
- ACL/SCO: `.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:252-298`

Ownership rules:

- Sender allocates HCI body.
- Receiver consumes it from the pointer.
- Receiver eventually sends `HCI_FREE_PKT` back to the allocating core.
- Allocating core frees the pointer after receiving `HCI_FREE_PKT`.

For CP-originated events/ACL:

- CP allocates.
- AP consumes.
- AP sends `HCI_FREE_PKT`.
- CP frees at `.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:464-469`.

For AP-originated commands:

- AP allocates.
- CP consumes.
- CP sends `HCI_FREE_PKT`.
- AP frees at `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:441-446`.

## 8.4 Cache and barriers

The formal mailbox uses a system data barrier before publishing:

- AP formal send: `.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:229-233`
- AP physical receive before copying: `.../bk7258_mbox0.c:254-255`

The vendor CP mailbox adapter uses cache clean before publishing a stable slot:

`.../cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mbox0_adapter.c:423-430`.

The vendor generic IPC code uses cache flush and `__DMB()` when copying swap-region data:

`.../cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc_cmd.c:160-169`, `:204-213`, and `:277-284`.

For the Bluetooth pointer transport, the implementation must ensure:

1. HCI body contents are visible before publishing its pointer.
2. The 16-byte descriptor is visible before publishing its envelope pointer.
3. The receiver invalidates/flushes as required by the actual cache configuration before dereferencing the cross-core HCI pointer.
4. The HCI body remains allocated until the receiver has finished using it and returned `HCI_FREE_PKT`.

The existing vendor BT code does not show explicit cache maintenance around the HCI heap buffers. It relies on the underlying mailbox/memory configuration. That assumption must be verified for the OpenVela AP heap and the Armino CP heap.

# 9. Likely formal implementation shape

The minimum transport-side changes are conceptually:

## 9.1 Add formal channel constants

In the formal mailbox header, alongside the existing channel constants:

```c
#define BK7258_MB_CHAN_BT_CMD_TX  0x13u
#define BK7258_MB_CHAN_BT_CMD_RX  0x43u
```

The existing definitions are at:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:73-82`.

## 9.2 Add TX/RX channel slots

In:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:24-25,105-120`

extend:

```c
MB_CHANNEL_COUNT       5 -> 6
MB_RX_CHANNEL_COUNT    4 -> 5
```

and append Bluetooth after the existing UART/SARADC entries.

Appending is preferable because `g_channels[4]` is treated as the UART channel by the probe worker at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:953-965`.

## 9.3 Register a Bluetooth RX callback

Use:

```c
bk7258_mailbox_register_rx(
    BK7258_MB_CHAN_BT_CMD_RX,
    bluetooth_mailbox_rx,
    context);
```

The registration API is:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:247-251`

and implemented at:

`.../bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1109-1121`.

The callback should decode the raw 16-byte message as:

```c
hci_hdr_t
```

or an equivalent explicitly sized local structure, not as a formal generic payload message.

The callback must:

- validate `pkt_type`
- extract `hdr_ptr`
- enqueue `{pkt_type, hdr_ptr}`
- return `OK` only if queued
- return `-EAGAIN` if queue capacity is unavailable

## 9.4 Send Bluetooth packets through `0x13`

The AP-side formal Bluetooth adapter should construct a zeroed 16-byte raw descriptor, populate:

```text
word 1 = HCI packet type
word 2 = 32-bit HCI buffer pointer
```

and send it with:

```c
bk7258_mailbox_send_wire(
    BK7258_MB_CHAN_BT_CMD_TX,
    &message,
    callback,
    arg);
```

The formal send API is at:

`.../hardware/bk7258_mbox.h:245-251`.

For a normal vendor-compatible command, the transport command byte can be set to zero unless a particular Armino command ID is required. The vendor BT RX path switches on `pkt_type`, not on `hdr.cmd`:

- AP RX switch: `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:53-143`
- CP RX switch: `.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:56-146`

The formal transport itself will add sequence and logical-channel fields.

## 9.5 Preserve the vendor packet worker model

Do not call the full Bluetooth stack from the formal mailbox RX callback. The vendor implementation only queues a small message from the RX callback and processes it in a task:

- AP queueing: `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:53-143`
- AP worker: `.../ap/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:325-478`
- CP queueing: `.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:56-146`
- CP worker: `.../cp/components/bk_bluetooth/ipc/src/bt_ipc_core.c:328-501`

This is especially important because the formal RX callback is reached while IRQs are disabled:

- `
